commits.summary: Brief for a feature loop that makes build.py a runner of claims, attempts and evidence
commits.body:
Adds llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration-review.md, an outside review of examples/tools/build.py at 4c279ba6 kept verbatim as the loop's fixed input. It finds that a crashed verifier counts as a counterexample, D1 can check an old contract against new bytecode, missing TLC coverage reads as none, and several properties collapse into one statement. It proposes a claim/attempt/conclusion/evidence format and four developer features: check this bug fix, JVM replay with a JUnit test, external artifacts as inputs, and proof experiments.

Adds llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md, the brief feature-loop.sh runs. It cuts the review's five phases into 14 steps of about one cycle (1a-5b), each with an acceptance criterion. It sets the working rules (runner tests with mocked subprocesses in a new examples/tools/test_build.py, proofs queued through the pipeline, recorded results never edited by hand, nothing weakened), four open questions for the user with the default the loop takes, Progress, Loop settings (new session f1a97af5, claude-opus-5-5, high effort) and Loop until.

commits.summary: build-orchestration brief: Phase 4's developer features deferred
commits.body:
By the user's decision, the review's developer-facing features (check this bug fix, JVM replay with a JUnit test, external artifacts as inputs) move out of the plan into a Deferred section kept for context. They would add considerations that are useful to developers but not novel, and make the proof experiments harder to run; they will be revisited separately. The brief now states its focus: data structures, interfaces and evaluations for proof work, built so that such features can later be added as renderings of evidence already held. Step 3b gains typed witness values, target descriptors, argument mappings and artifact identities for that reason. Phase 5 follows Phase 3. The two open questions that belonged to Phase 4 moved with it, and the Done-when table drops its row.

Verified by reading the brief's headings and cross-references after the move; no code changed.

commits.summary: build-orchestration brief: Phase 5's proof experiments deferred
commits.body:
By the user's decision, Phase 5 (experiment profiles, diagnosis, resumption and the agent-driven loop) moves out of the plan into its own Deferred section, ahead of Phase 4's, since it will likely come first. The structural work comes before it, with more design and planning informed by what Phases 1-3 settle. The loop now covers Phases 1-3 only. The brief says what those phases should leave room for (stable claim ids, attempts with effective settings, narrowed claims as new claims, status and failure reasons as data), and that step 2b's per-configuration TLC checkpoints stay in scope as a correctness fix. The open question on where the AI loop lives moved with Phase 5. Done when drops its row. Loop until says the deferred phases are never a reason to go on.

Verified by reading the brief's headings and cross-references after the move; no code changed.

commits.summary: build.py: how a verifier's run ended is decided before its verdict (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 1a of the build-orchestration brief. Before, build.py classified a jvmcontract or Java-verifier run as verified on exit 0, unverifiable when the output said 'cannot be verified', and violation otherwise. A verifier killed by signal 9 with empty output was recorded as 'Violation: counterexample found', with no counterexample, and matched an example that expected a violation. write_evidence() also wrote an empty SARIF report when the verifier wrote none. The review's findings were checked against the code at c4fa2f64 and all still held.

Now execution_status() and conclude() (and tlc_conclusion() for TLC, run directly for Box Office or through jvmcontract tlc --json) first record result.execution: completed, timed-out, killed (a negative code or 128+N), invalid-output (nothing printed, malformed JSON, exit 1 with no evidence or no report) or tool-error (any other exit code; a TLC run that ended without a verdict). Only a completed run has a verdict. A violation needs the evidence the runner read (counterexamples, changed cases, capability or boundary changes, new ! lines, a trace) and the verifier's SARIF report. A run without a verdict records verdict null, the label '⚠ No verdict: <reason>' and expectation not-evaluable, and matchesExpected is false. build.py exits 1 and prints a line the pipeline's example:unexpected signal matches. The runs that give the verdict are recorded, not fatal, on exit code 2. Setup steps (update, tla, compile) still stop the runner, now also on a signal. A missing report is not made up, and a stale result.sarif or statement.java from an earlier run is removed, so a folder never shows another run's evidence. Each D1 configuration also records its status. The page of a run without a verdict says so in place of the findings.

Choices: a run that did not complete gets verdict null, not 'unverifiable'. That is the option that reports less, and otherwise a crash would match example 003, which expects unverifiable. 'Why the verdict is right' still prints the authored explanation; separating it from the observed evidence is step 3c. The per-configuration termination reason beyond the status is step 2b.

Verified: the new examples/tools/test_build.py (25 unittest cases, mocked processes) covers signal 9 with empty output, 137 and 134, exit codes 2/3/101, timeouts, empty output, exit 1 without evidence or report, malformed TLC JSON, TLC killed or late inside the tool, a violation without a trace, rendering and schema validation of a no-verdict result, and main()'s exit code and pipeline signal. Recomputing every recorded result's expectation under the new rule gives exactly what was recorded, and every recorded violation has its evidence. All 140 committed results validate against the extended schema, which accepts the old shape. verification/test_pipeline.py passes. build.py --render-only renders every page. Eight pages changed only because they had drifted from their committed results (timings, and a renderer sentence on 110); nothing in them comes from this change.

Verification jobs, one per approach, check that the verdicts are unchanged and that result.json gains execution: 20261105-112331-example-126-b9-under-build-py-s-executio (B9 JBMC), 20261105-112331-example-132-b9-under-build-py-s-executio (B9 native), 20261105-112331-example-017-b11-under-build-py-s-executi (B11), 20261105-112331-example-110-b12-under-build-py-s-executi (B12), 20261105-112331-example-101-d1-under-build-py-s-executio (D1), 20261105-112331-example-003-b8-under-build-py-s-executio (B8 Box Office, expected unverifiable).
